page.layout: One column of running text, with two medallion engravings above it side by side (left: Vitellius, right: Petronia). A small medallion engraving stands at the left beside the last two paragraphs, which wrap around it. No marginal notes. Running head at top, page number at top left.

main_text.l: AVLVS Vitellius, à Galba in inferiorem Germaniā mis-
sus est. Aduentantem, male animatus erga principē exercitus,
libens ac supinis manibus excipit, velut dono Deūm oblatum
III.Conf.filiū, ætate integra, facili ac prodigo animo. hāc de se
veterē persuasione auxerat, tota ipse via milites obuios exoscu-
latus, pérq; diuersoria comis, manè singulos iámne ientassent
scifcitatus, séque fecisse, rustu quoque ostédens. nil cuiquā ne-
gauit, atq; etiā vltro reis fordes, dānatis supplicia dēpsit: Quare
vixdū mense transacto, subitò à militibus è cubiculo raptus, vt
erat, in veste domestica, Imperator consalutatur anno mundi
4031.à Christo nato 69. Hic in ientacula, prādia & cœnas, faci-
lè omnibus sufficiebat vomitandi cõsuetudine. Cœna ei data
est aduentitia à fratre, in qua, super cæteros sumptus, 2000.le-
ctissimorū pisciū 7000.auium apposita sunt. hāc quoque exu-
perauit ipse, dedicatione patinæ, quam clipeum Minervæ dictita-
bat.Sæuus fuit, nam & eius hæc vox est, optimè olere occisum hostē,
& melius ciuem. Vespasiano principe declarato, cœno fimóque
iactatus, vestéque discissa in forum tractus, subiecto ad mentū
gladio, tandem minutis.ictibus excarnificatus, vnco trahitur
in Tyberim.Suet.in Vitell.vixit an.57.rexit menses 8.
PETRONIA Confularis viri filia, Vitellij vxor prior, Pe-
tronianū altero captum oculo peperit, quem pater interemisse
creditur, infimulatum parricidij, post
matris obitum.
GALERIA Fundana, A.Vitellij
vxor, Prætorio patre nata, liberos vtrius-
que sexus tulit, sed marem titubantia
oris prope mutum.Suet.in Vitell.

page.notes: The upper engravings are medallion portraits of Vitellius (left) and Petronia (right), with circular legends around them; the legends are engraved and only partly legible at this scan, so they are not transcribed. The small medallion beside the last paragraphs is a portrait of Galeria Fundana, with a legend around the rim, also not transcribed. "minutis.ictibus" in the Vitellius paragraph: the letter after "minuti" is read as s, possibly f; not certain. Printed spacing "Suet.in", "Vitell.vixit", "an.57.rexit" follows the print as seen.
